thread:
maya: Heads-up — planning to decommission the old dev keystore next Tue. Found an outstanding deletion request that references customer snapshots encrypted under that key. Need ops + legal input.
jonah: which key exactly? can we just rotate instead of destroy?
maya: key path: cloud-kms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/keys/dev-legacy. Snapshots are in s3://redwood-backups/prod/snap-2023-*. ~120 objects.
leah-legal: if the DSAR targets personal data in those snapshots, destroying the key would make them unrecoverable — that may satisfy erasure but we need a defensible attestation with timelines. Also check any ongoing legal holds.
sam-privacy: quick thought: two options — (A) preserve key and run forensics to extract & delete customer rows, then rotate key; (B) destroy key and produce attestation that key destruction renders data inaccessible. Option A is long and noisy.
jonah: re-encrypting requires access to plaintext. We'd have to spin up restore infra, mount snapshots, run scrubbing job, then re-encrypt and re-upload. Costly and risky.
maya: also flagged in vuln triage: key hasn't rotated in 28 months and IAM has broad bindings (internal-engineering). Sec wants either rotate + tighten RBAC before we keep it, or schedule decommission ASAP.
leah-legal: if we go with destruction, legal needs a written acceptance from product that the customer consents to irrecoverable deletion OR that there is no active legal hold. I'll draft a checklist.
jonah: technical mitigation if we keep it: restrict IAM to service accounts only, enable key access audit logs, and create a retention exception ticket with TTL (30d) so we have time to scrub.
maya: sample IAM change I'll run if agreed:
```
# pseudo
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding dev-legacy \
  --member=serviceAccount:backup-restore@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```
maya: ops-bot created a tracking issue INC-1234 and a retention-exception request REQ-4521 :eyes:
ops-bot: incident INC-1234 created by maya, priority P2, assignees: jonah, sam-privacy
sam-privacy: proposed playbook: 1) pause decommission, 2) lock IAM, 3) enable audit exports to secure bucket, 4) attempt targeted restore for affected customer IDs (if feasible), 5) if restore impossible, proceed with key destruction + legal attestation.
leah-legal: that playbook sounds fine. Legal will confirm required attestation language and check for holds by EOD.
jonah: I'll scope restore cost and time today and post numbers in INC-1234.
maya: ok. Owners: jonah (tech lead), sam-privacy (privacy lead), leah-legal (legal). I'll block decommission until we have signoffs or 72h TTL on the retention exception. Thanks.
